reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in extending the UU (Uplift and Upsample) architecture to jointly predict 3D joint locations and rotations in a single forward pass. The method compares rotation representations—axis-angle (AA), quaternions (Q), and rotation matrices (RM)—and loss functions—MSE and geodesic—to optimize performance. Rotation matrices with geodesic loss yield the best results, while quaternions fail under geodesic loss due to non-Euclidean geometry. The SMPL-X layer approach integrates rotation predictions into a differentiable body model, linking rotations to joint positions. Weak supervision via pseudo-labels or VPoser priors enables training without ground-truth rotations. The failure modes include catastrophic quaternion collapse under geodesic loss, degradation under weak supervision, and runtime inefficiencies in real-time deployment. The method achieves 150× speedup over traditional IK methods, making it suitable for real-time biomechanical analysis in sports broadcasting.
